title: Work with and look after materials in the production process

lessons.title: Receiving and identifying materials
lessons.html:
Receiving and identifying materials

In grain handling and milling, materials include the grain itself, plus bags, pallets, fumigants, lubricants, spare parts, packaging and cleaning chemicals. Every material costs money. Looking after materials means using the right material for the job, in the right amount, and keeping it in good condition so nothing is wasted or contaminated.

Receiving materials

  1. Check the documents. Compare the delivery note with the order: product, grade, quantity, batch number.
  2. Check the condition. Look for torn bags, wet patches, broken pallets, leaking containers, insects or mould in grain.
  3. Check quantity. Count units or weigh on the weighbridge or platform scale.
  4. Record differences. Write any shortage or damage on the delivery note before signing, and tell your supervisor.
  5. Label and identify. Each batch must be clearly marked so it can be traced and used in the right order.

Know the material

Before you work with a material, know:

  • What it is used for and what grade or specification it is.
  • How it must be stored: dry, cool, off the floor, away from other products.
  • Its hazards. Read the label and the safety data sheet (SDS) for chemicals, fumigants and lubricants.
  • Its shelf life or expiry date.

Example

A truck delivers 2 000 new woven polypropylene bags. The supervisor counts the bales and finds one bale wet from a leaking tarpaulin on the truck. She writes this on the delivery note, sets the wet bale aside for return, and stores the rest on pallets in the dry store. Wet bags would have gone mouldy and spoiled the grain packed in them.

Grain is a food and feed product. Any material that touches it must be clean and suitable for food contact. Never use chemical containers, fuel drums or dirty bags for grain.

lessons.title: Storing, issuing and using materials
lessons.html:
Storing, issuing and using materials

Good storage

  • Store on pallets, off the floor and away from walls so air can move and pests can be seen.
  • Keep the store dry, clean and free of rodents and birds.
  • Keep chemicals and fumigants in a separate, locked, ventilated store with warning signs. Never store them with grain, bags or food.
  • Keep fuel and lubricants away from heat and ignition sources, with a fire extinguisher nearby.
  • Stack safely: not too high, heavy items at the bottom, stacks straight.
  • Label shelves and bins so items are easy to find.

Stock rotation

Use first in, first out (FIFO): the oldest stock is used first. For grain and anything with an expiry date, this prevents spoilage. Check dates at every stock count.

Issuing materials

  1. Issue only against a requisition or job card.
  2. Record what was issued, how much, to whom and for which job.
  3. Issue the correct grade. The wrong lubricant or the wrong fumigant dose can damage machines or grain.

Using materials in production

  • Use only the amount needed. Return unused material to the store and record it.
  • Keep materials off the floor in the work area.
  • Clean up spilt grain quickly. Spills attract pests and can be a slipping and dust hazard.
  • Report damaged, contaminated or suspect material instead of using it.

Waste and the environment

  • Sort waste: scrap metal, plastic, paper, used oil.
  • Used oil and chemical containers must be disposed of as your site procedure says, never burnt or dumped in the veld.
  • Damaged grain may be sold as feed or disposed of; ask your supervisor.

Safety

Lift bags correctly, use trolleys and forklifts only if trained, and wear PPE when handling chemicals. Grain dust can explode in confined spaces, so keep dust down and follow no-smoking rules.

Key points

  • Check documents, condition and quantity when materials arrive.
  • Store materials clean, dry, off the floor and chemicals separately.
  • Use first in, first out.
  • Issue and record materials against a job card.
  • Report damaged or contaminated material and dispose of waste correctly.
